items.question: How do I install TrayNook?
paragraphs: Install TrayNook with our Homebrew tap, or download it from GitHub Releases.
Open the app, grant Accessibility permission, and arrange icons in Settings → Layout.

Public builds default to ad-hoc signing; Apple notarization is optional. macOS may require System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway after you first try opening the app. Follow Apple’s instructions.

items.question: What permissions does it need?
paragraphs: Accessibility is required. Screen Recording is optional, for menu-bar icon previews. Updates may require Accessibility approval again.
Launch at Login is optional in Settings → General. The app interface is in English.

items.question: Will it work on my Mac?
paragraphs: Packaged for Apple silicon and Intel. Support targets stable macOS majors receiving Apple security updates, on a best-effort basis.
The technical minimum is macOS 13.0, not a tested compatibility guarantee.

items.question: Can every menu-bar item be moved?
paragraphs: Some items cannot be moved. Protected system items and items TrayNook cannot safely identify stay visible. Behavior can vary with the app and display setup.
Report an issue if something does not behave as expected. Review diagnostics before sharing them.

items.question: What about privacy and updates?
paragraphs: Layouts and preferences stay on your Mac. TrayNook sends no analytics, application inventory, or screenshots.

Update checks and downloads contact GitHub over HTTPS, exposing usual request metadata and your IP address. Automatic checks default on; automatic downloads default off. Disable Check for updates automatically to stop background checks.
You approve installation with Install & Relaunch.
